title: LeanForth check report, schema version 0.1
description: What `leanforth check --json EXPORT` prints: one JSON text, then a line feed. The export staged and fed to the checker, every declaration's verdict in input order, read after the run from the slots of the checked environment the run made, the counts, the exit status, the fuel used, the input's size and, apart in `measured`, the times and memory. Written by src/cli/check-json.fs; documented in docs/user/COMMAND_LINE.md, section JSON output. A report, not a record: it names no commit and no SHA-256 (run records do, docs/programming/RUN_RECORDS.md), and nothing ever reads it back into a check.
$comment: Uses only the keywords that tests/support/schema_subset.py implements; it refuses any other keyword. Every member but `measured` is deterministic: the same on every run of the same export with the same options and the same build. Numbers are integers within I-JSON's exact range. Version 0.1 is untrusted and has not passed the [format] gate. Rules no keyword of the subset can state, which tests/cli/test_leanforth.py checks on every report it makes: when `counts` is an object, `counts.declarations` equals the number of items of `declarations` and the sum of the eight verdict counts (accepted to notChecked), each verdict count equals the number of declarations with that verdict, and `counts.notProved` the number with `notProved` true; `fuel.unknown` equals the number of declarations whose fuel is null and `fuel.total` the sum of the others' fuel; `fuel.top` is in order of fuel, most first, each entry's fuel and verdict those of the declaration at its index; `input.declarations` equals `counts.declarations`.

export.description: The export's file name as the command line gave it, with the escapes of names (src/cli/name-text.fs): a backslash as \\, a character the text rule bans as \u{X}, a byte that is not UTF-8 as \x{X}.

manifest.description: checked: the export was read only if it matched EXPORT.manifest.json (the default); not-checked: --no-manifest.

fuel.description: Fuel each declaration's check starts with (--fuel).

dependencyPool.description: The room the run's dependency pool starts with; it grows (not a limit since plan task 6.2.0).

run.description: The run's outcome: ok when every declaration's slot ended final; not-run when the export was not read.

stopped.description: true when the run stopped on an internal fault (a check threw, or publishing failed): the declaration where it stopped is invalid, and those after it are not checked.

declarations.description: Every declaration in input order, when the run's environment could be read; none otherwise.

counts.description: The declarations by verdict; null when no verdict could be read.

input.description: The input as fed to the checker; null when it was not.

exitStatus.description: The command's exit status: 0 all accepted, 1 something rejected, 2 unsupported or unknown, 3 a resource limit, 4 malformed input, 5 an internal fault, 6 all accepted but some NOT PROVED (proposed, pending the owner's confirmation at this format's gate); the most severe of 5, 4, 1, 3, 2, 6, 0 wins.

allOf.description: An export that was not read was not checked.
Declarations are listed exactly when they are counted.
A run that ended ok made every slot final: no declaration is not-checked.
Exit status 0 only when the run ended ok, did not stop, listed at least one declaration and every declaration was accepted and proved: every other count is 0, and every fuel is known.
Exit status 6 only when every declaration was accepted and at least one is NOT PROVED.
A NOT PROVED declaration never leaves the status 0.
A rejected declaration makes the status 1 unless a worse one (4, 5) wins.
An invalid declaration makes the status 4, or 5.
A declaration not checked means the run stopped on an internal fault.
A run that stopped on an internal fault has status 5 and did not end ok; one that never ran did not stop.

allAccepted.description: Counts in which every declaration was accepted: at least one, and none with another verdict.

verdict.description: accepted for a slot made final with outcome ok; another outcome's name for any other final slot, and invalid for one whose check began but did not end final; not-checked for one the run never reached.

name.description: A declaration's name as the term printer writes it.

read.description: Reading the export: its outcome and, for a failure, the phase that failed (open: the file did not open; stage: the importer stage, with the line, field and reason of the NDJSON reader or the manifest check, line 0 for the manifest and for sealing; feed: giving the stage to the checker, with the number of the expression or declaration where it stopped).

diagnostic.description: What the failed check recorded: the reason code and its name (docs/programming/DIAGNOSTICS.md), the site (module and word, or empty), its two numbers, and the step reached: check-block's for a member of an inductive block, else check-declaration's.

index.description: The declaration's position in the input, from 0.

axiomBits.description: The axiom set read from the accepted slot, as bits; 0 for none. The first checker accepts no axiom, so it is always 0 today.

notProved.description: true for an accepted declaration that depends on an axiom: Lean's verdict, labelled NOT PROVED and never counted as proved (owner, 2026-11-04).

fuel.description: Fuel the declaration's check used: exact for an accepted one (with that budget it is accepted, with one less not) and the budget for an exhausted one; 0 for a member of an inductive block after its first, whose check is the first's, and for one not checked; null when not known, for a check that ended with no fuel left without running out (a failed inference gives its counter up).

notProved.description: Accepted declarations that are NOT PROVED (counted among accepted too).

total.description: Fuel used by every check of the run whose use is known.

unknown.description: Declarations whose fuel used is not known (null fuel).

top.description: The declarations that used the most fuel, most first, those of equal fuel in input order; none that used none.

input.description: The input as fed: declarations, term nodes, levels and constant references in the checker's stores, and names in the stage.

measured.description: Not deterministic: wall and CPU time of each phase and of the whole run so far, in microseconds (null on a host without clocks; 0 for a phase that did not run), the peak resident memory of the process in bytes (VmHWM of /proc/self/status; null where the host does not give it) and the bytes of heap blocks the stage held (null when nothing was staged).
